translated: When you put 3 credits for HSC it does not encourage average students to work more. The bright ones will stay on top of them. Many of those with 3 credits have to do 3 years instead of 2 years HSC to get a correct result otherwise the result is weak in most cases. For university you need to have a good background. There may be 1 or 2 exceptions but generally no. I guarantee the success rate will drop again next year. The amount of resources that a parent needs and that the state spends I think it is better for 3 credits to go to polytechnic or technical because in three years there you come out with a certificate that allows instant employability. input: Moi mo pointe bann ministre inn tro malever. Zot donne zot lopital gratis, fer zot aret peye minisipalite, donne zot pension invalide mem seki pa merite. Seki merite bizin pa dan bord. Pu bann ebouers, zot mérite enn respe par tu bann fami dan Maurice. Ki soi Navin ou Ramgoolam, zot lizye kot zot ki ale vini dan Europe, zot pa pran leson pu met enn lalwa sever dan sa lil Maurice la. Zot pe fer piquer pu bann lisyin, me pa pu bann dimunn ki pa pe respe lanvironnman dan zot lakaz. Moi mo bien sagren kan mo truve tusala bann dimunn kinn pose kandida pu minisipalite. Mo dir zot ki bann ministre mem ek bann seki elu dan bann minisipalite, kan prosenn eleksion vini zot ava kone ki mo pu fer ar zot. Bann bon nanyin ki kone zis zot pos, zot pe tire sa tigit la. Moi, moi zot bann ministre dan nu ti lil la.
translated: I am pointing fingers at the ministers because they have gone too far. They give out free hospital care, stop people from paying municipal fees, and grant disability pensions even to those who do not deserve them. Those who truly deserve it are left aside. As for the garbage collectors, they deserve respect from every family in Mauritius. Whether it is Navin or Ramgoolam, their eyes are fixed on those who travel back and forth to Europe, yet they do not learn any lessons to introduce stricter laws in this little island of Mauritius. They are enforcing fines for dogs, but not for people who do not respect the environment around their homes. I am very saddened when I see all these people standing as candidates for the municipalities. I am telling the ministers and those elected to the municipalities that when the next election comes, they will find out what I will do. Those good-for-nothings who only care about their own pockets are taking advantage of the situation. Me, I am talking about those ministers in our little island.

Even when we are enjoying ourselves, I do not leave my child alone, not even for a minute or a second. Every five to ten minutes, I look for my child or call to check whether they are there. That is how I see it.
